name: hra-3d-crosswalk
title: HRA 3D Crosswalk — Full ASCT+B-3D Anatomical-Structure Tree
question:
Does the HRA CDN's ASCT+B-3D models crosswalk load into a Step-driven
composite, giving the full 1,400+ anatomical-structure (AS) tree — not
just the ~81 per-organ reference-organ GLBs — with resolvable Uberon CURIEs
and source-organ GLB names?

study_card.goal: Fetch the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk CSV via HRACrosswalkStep and confirm the composite loads a non-empty, Uberon-annotated anatomical-structure list.
study_card.mechanism: HRACrosswalkStep.update -> fetch_crosswalk(CROSSWALK_URL) -> parse CSV rows after the `anatomical_structure_of` header -> one store -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: 1,400+ anatomical-structure rows load, most with a resolvable Uberon CURIE (`mesh` rows) and some `organizational` rows with no Uberon, each carrying its source-organ GLB name and parent node.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is the crosswalk's Uberon coverage complete/stable enough to key organ-granularity model coverage off of (Task B), or does its `organizational`/missing-Uberon fraction undercut that?

biological_summary:
The Human Reference Atlas (HRA) publishes ~81 whole-organ 3D reference
models (per-sex GLB scenes), but a mechanistic model rarely maps cleanly
onto a whole organ — it targets a lobe, duct, nephron segment, or other
sub-organ anatomical structure (AS). The ASCT+B-3D models crosswalk is the
HRA's digital object that cuts each reference-organ GLB into its
constituent AS scene nodes and keys each to a Uberon CURIE where the node
is directly ontology-representable (`mesh` node type), leaving purely
structural grouping nodes (`organizational`) unkeyed. This is the
substrate every downstream HRA-3D coverage/linkage step (Tasks B and C)
crosses against the BioModels-derived organ annotations, so its size,
Uberon-density, and organ span set the ceiling on how fine-grained model
coverage can ever be reported.
readouts: fraction of rows with a resolvable UBERON: CURIE (vs organizational/empty)
count of distinct source-organ GLBs referenced

report.title: HRA 3D Crosswalk — full ASCT+B-3D anatomical-structure tree loads
report.objective:
Does the HRA CDN's ASCT+B-3D models crosswalk load into a Step-driven
composite, giving the full anatomical-structure (AS) tree with
resolvable Uberon CURIEs and source-organ GLB names?
report.conclusion:
The live composite loads 2,295 anatomical-structure rows spanning 116
distinct source-organ GLBs (both sexes). 1,730/2,295 rows (75.4%) carry
a resolvable UBERON: CURIE (`node_type=mesh`, 1,410 rows) or
`surface` (464 rows); the remaining 419 `organizational` rows (18.3%,
plus 2 blank) are pure grouping nodes with no Uberon and are correctly
excluded from coverage computation (`coverage.build_coverage` skips
rows with an empty `uberon`). This exceeds the ~1,400+ AS nodes
originally estimated and comfortably clears the ~81-reference-organ
floor, confirming the crosswalk gives materially finer anatomical
granularity than the whole-organ GLBs alone.
report.caveat:
Uberon coverage is real but partial (75.4%, not 100%) — the
`organizational` fraction (18.3%) is structurally un-keyable (they are
grouping nodes, not anatomy), so organ-granularity coverage
(`model-coverage-3d`/`corpus-coverage`) can never reach 100% of raw
crosswalk rows even with a complete model corpus; this is a data-model
ceiling, not a bug.

evidence.summary: 2,295 rows loaded, 116 source-organ GLBs; 1,730/2,295 (75.4%) UBERON-keyed (1,410 mesh + 464 surface rows); 419 organizational rows (18.3%) structurally un-keyable.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline live fetch and CSV parse of the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk completed without error.

biological_validation.basis: The endpoint returns the expected data shape/counts (2,295 rows, exceeding the ~1,400+ estimate) with 75.4% resolvable to Uberon -- the Step-based fetch is accurate to the live crosswalk.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 quantifies the 75.4% Uberon-density ceiling that bounds every downstream organ-granularity coverage computation (model-coverage-3d, corpus-coverage).

limitations: The 18.3% organizational-row fraction is structurally un-keyable (pure grouping nodes, not anatomy), so downstream organ-granularity coverage can never reach 100% of raw crosswalk rows even with a complete model corpus -- a data-model ceiling, not a bug.

resolved_uncertainties: The crosswalk exceeds the original ~1,400+ AS-node estimate (2,295 rows / 1,730 Uberon-keyed), confirming it gives materially finer granularity than the 81 whole-organ GLBs.
remaining_uncertainties: Can the 18.3% organizational/unkeyed rows ever be resolved to Uberon, or is that a permanent ceiling on organ-granularity coverage?

followup_study_proposals.title: Resolve organizational-row Uberon gap
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Attempt to Uberon-key the ~18% organizational/un-keyed crosswalk rows (or confirm the ceiling), improving the AS coverage denominator.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: For each of the 419 `organizational` crosswalk rows, check whether its `parent`/`label` or an adjacent `mesh`/`surface` sibling node resolves to a Uberon CURIE it could inherit, and report how many of the 18.3% un-keyed rows are recoverable vs a genuine structural-grouping ceiling.
